title: Viscoelastic oil drop pushed through water: Hadamard-Rybczynski drag in a spherical cell (frequency response, mixed u-p, analytic)
description:
An optical push on an oil drop in water, idealised: a drop of radius a = 1 um at the centre of a spherical water cell of radius b = 5 a with a no-slip wall, driven along the axis by a uniform body_force f = F_b / (4/3 pi a^3) on the drop (F_b = 1 pN, as an optical force would act), axisymmetric (r, z), azimuthal order 0 (x = r, the axis on x_lo, the centre at z_c). solid_mechanics on quadratic triangles, formulation mixed (Taylor-Hood: P2 displacement, P1 pressure per material): water (library viscosity mu_o = 1.002e-3 Pa s) and the drop are both incompressible liquids (no bulk modulus), two touching incompressible groups: the pressure is duplicated on the interface (it may jump there) and the pair, enclosed by the held wall, gets one joined gauge pin. The drop is a Maxwell liquid: viscosity mu_inf = 1e-5 Pa s plus a Prony branch G_1 = 50 Pa, tau = 1 ms (zero-shear viscosity mu_0 = 0.05 Pa s: below ~100 Hz a Newtonian 0.05 Pa s oil), so G_i* = j w mu_inf + G_1 j w tau / (1 + j w tau) and G_o* = j w mu_o (exp(+j w t)); the ratio s = G_i* / G_o* = (mu_inf + G_1 tau / (1 + j w tau)) / mu_o runs from 50 - 3j (a nearly rigid drop, 10 Hz) through complex values (an elastic drop, 1-100 kHz) to 0.01 - 0.008j (bubble-like, 1 MHz), so one sweep of 21 log-spaced frequencies 10 Hz - 1 MHz goes from rigid to bubble. The wall: the window outside the circle of radius b (object 'wall' = box minus cell) is an elastic material (E 1 MPa, compressible: a fully held incompressible zone would be a singular pressure block) held by fixed_domain, so the arc is a no-slip wall (the outer-face supports act on window edges only).
Quasi-static: every density is rho_q = 1e-6 kg/m^3, so w rho b^2 / mu_o < 2e-7 and w^2 rho a^2 / |G_i*| < 1e-6 at 1 MHz and the flow is creeping (Stokes), as the reference assumes (rho_q = 1e-3 moves Phi by 1e-5 at 1 MHz: linear in rho). With real densities (~1e3 kg/m^3) inertia (Basset memory, added mass) shifts Phi by 3e-5 of |Phi| at 10 Hz, 3e-3 at 1 kHz, 3 % at 10 kHz and 34 % at 100 kHz: rerun with rho_q = 998 to see it; this reference then no longer applies.
No surface tension: the interface carries no capillary stress. At linear order this changes nothing here: a uniform force on a sphere excites only the l = 1 (translation) shape mode, which costs no interface area, so a tension gamma would only add the static Laplace jump 2 gamma / a to the drop pressure (a constant, absorbed by the drop's pressure level) and leave every displacement unchanged; the drop stays spherical because the cos(theta) part of the normal-stress jump is balanced by the body force, as in Hadamard-Rybczynski. Left out: surfactant (Marangoni) stresses, which immobilise a real interface and make a drop drag like a rigid sphere, and large deformations.
Analytic (derived for this cell; Stokes stream function psi = sin^2(theta) f(r), lab frame, wall at rest; u_r = 2 cos(theta) f / r^2, u_theta = -sin(theta) f' / r): f_o = A r^4 + B r^2 + C r + D / r in the water, f_i = E r^4 + F r^2 in the drop; f_o(b) = f_o'(b) = 0 (no slip), f_o(a) = f_i(a) = X a^2 / 2 (the interface translates by X, the displacement of the drop pole theta = 0), f_o'(a) = f_i'(a) (tangential continuity) and G_o* (-f_o'' / a + 2 f_o' / a^2 - 2 f_o / a^3) = G_i* (the same of f_i) at r = a (shear stress). By correspondence (velocity j w u, every viscosity mu -> G* / (j w)) this is the Stokes system for the displacement. The water's force on the drop is -8 pi G_o* C, and the cos(theta) normal-stress balance with the body force (gamma = 0) is the global balance F_b = 8 pi G_o* C. Result: X = F_b / (2 pi a G_o* Phi), Phi = (P0 + P1 s) / (Q0 + Q1 s), lam = a / b: P0 = 8 + 12 lam^5, P1 = 12 (1 - lam^5), Q0 = 4 - 6 lam + 6 lam^5 - 4 lam^6, Q1 = 4 - 9 lam + 10 lam^3 - 9 lam^5 + 4 lam^6. lam -> 0 gives Hadamard-Rybczynski Phi = (2 + 3 s) / (1 + s), i.e. F = -2 pi a G_o* X (2 G_o* + 3 G_i*) / (G_o* + G_i*) (6 pi rigid, 4 pi bubble); s -> infinity Cunningham's rigid sphere in a sphere 3 (1 - lam^5) / (1 - 9/4 lam + 5/2 lam^3 - 9/4 lam^5 + lam^6); s = 0 Haberman and Sayre's bubble 2 (1 + 3/2 lam^5) / (1 - 3/2 lam + 3/2 lam^5 - lam^6). At lam = 0.2 the wall raises the drag 1.76x (rigid) and 1.43x (bubble): without inertia the wall effect is O(a / R) (Stokeslet far field), so an unbounded reference would need an impractically large container; a box r < 5.5 a, |z| < 5.5 a was 2-10 % off this sphere formula. Inside, the Hill vortex: the drop-centre displacement u_c = 2 F, u_c / X = (Q1 s + N_c) / (Q1 s + Q0), and the equator (r = a, z = z_c) tangential displacement, along z, u_e = 4 E a^2 + 2 F, u_e / X = (Q1 s + N_e) / (Q1 s + Q0), N_c = (1 - lam)^2 (6 + 6 lam + 6 lam^2 + lam^3 - 4 lam^4), N_e = (1 - lam)^2 (2 - 2 lam - 6 lam^2 - 5 lam^3 - 4 lam^4) (unbounded: (s + 3/2) / (s + 1) and (s + 1/2) / (s + 1)). Checked by a symbolic solve: Stokes residuals 0 in both liquids, the stress integral equals -8 pi mu_o C, the normal-stress and force balances agree, the three limits above; the parameter formulas match a direct numeric 6 x 6 solve to 4e-14.
Derived curves tab: plot 'drag', Re and Im of Phi = F_b / (2 pi a G_o* X) from the pole probe over the closed form (Re Phi falls from 5.21 at 10 Hz, near the rigid 5.27, to 2.876 at 1 MHz, near the bubble 2.857; Im Phi dips to -1.15 near 6 kHz where the drop is elastic); plot 'inside', u_centre / X (1.017 to 1.694) and u_equator / X (0.983 to 0.306): the internal circulation grows as the drop softens. Curves & tables tab: the pole probe u_y_re / u_y_im (X itself, ~1 / f) with the closed form; the wall table F_y = -F_b (its F_x, the sum of the radial ring reactions, is no net force). Derived values tab: wall_force_ratio = F_y of the wall / F_b = -1 (equilibrium: the wall carries the whole body force; the error is the P2 isoparametric drop volume, ~h^4), Re Phi at 10 Hz and 1 MHz, u_centre / X and u_equator / X at 1 MHz (real parts). Field tab: u_abs, u_y and the pressure (p > 0 in compression, jumping across the interface; its level is set by the one gauge pin) at 1 MHz.
Expected agreement (h = a / 8 in the drop, a / 2 elsewhere, growth 1.25, 2,255 triangles; P2 is exact for the quadratic Hill vortex inside, the error comes from the water): curves 1.5e-4 to 7.7e-4 of their range, derived values 3e-5 to 1.8e-4, wall ratio 2.9e-7; tolerances 3-4x that. Mesh study h_drop = a / 4, a / 8, a / 16 (h_max a, a / 2, a / 4; 718, 2,255, 8,019 triangles): worst curve error 3.1e-3, 7.7e-4, 7.4e-5, wall ratio 4.8e-6, 2.9e-7, 1.6e-8; b = 10 a and a 4x thicker wall agree as well.
